content: Website Terms and Conditions Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000101329 A website's Terms of Use (also known as Terms and Conditions or Terms of Service) is basically a set of rules that users agree to follow when they interact with a website. Think of it as the "house rules" that the website owner sets to protect both themselves and the users. These terms cover everything from how the content on the site can be used, to what users can and can't do while they're there, and even what happens if someone violates those rules. Here's a quick rundown of what might be included: User Conduct : Guidelines on what behavior is acceptable or prohibited (e.g., no spamming, no illegal activities). Intellectual Property : Details about who owns the content on the site (text, images, videos) and how it can be used. Privacy : Information on how user data is collected, stored, and used by the website. Disclaimers : Statements that limit the website's liability for errors, inaccuracies, or damages that might occur from using the site. Governing Law : The legal jurisdiction that governs the terms (e.g., laws of a specific state or country). Termination : The right of the website owner to suspend or terminate a user's access for violating the terms. These terms create a legal framework that helps ensure everyone knows what’s expected, keeping the experience smooth and safe for all involved. Terms of Use Page All Brilliant Directories websites come with a Terms of Use page: domain.com /about/terms Example: https://www.demobootstrap.com/about/terms Accepting Terms of Use Users will agree to the Terms and Conditions upon sign up, whether it is a FREE or PAID account. Notes The Terms are accepted upon sign up once. Currently there is no setting to renew/accept Terms & Conditions agreement on a daily, weekly, monthly or yearly basis. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate?
